**Ida Abelman’s color pieces in the U.S. GSA Fine Arts Collection that are *not* lithographic prints**

| # | Title (GSA catalogue) | Year | Medium (as listed by GSA) | GSA Object ID |
|---|------------------------|------|---------------------------|--------------|
| 1 | **Countryside** | 1939 | *Color woodcut* on paper | 26755 (via art.gsa.gov) |

*All other color works that appear in the GSA inventory (“Construction”, “Under the Bridge”, “We Have a Claim!”, “Janitor’s Kids”, “Child Labor”, etc.) are recorded as lithographs and therefore do **not** meet the criteria.*

---

### Westernmost museum that holds the youngest of these works

The only non‑lithograph color work in the GSA collection is **“Countryside” (1939)**.  In the GSA’s public‑access database it is listed as being **on loan to the Cleveland Museum of Art** (Cleveland, Ohio).  Because there are no other GSA color‑printworks by Abelman that are not lithographs, the “youngest” (and only) such piece is held there.

**Answer:** The westernmost museum in which the youngest of the Ida Abelman color non‑lithograph works is held is **Cleveland Museum of Art**.

### Westernmost museum that holds the youngest of these works
